entities.name: George of Antioch
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
George of Antioch was a Greek Eastern Orthodox Christian from the Byzantine Empire who played a crucial role in shaping Norman Sicily's multicultural society and naval power during the 12th century. He served as an advisor to Roger II of Sicily, helping to establish the city-state as a major center of trade and commerce.

Born around 1050 in Antioch, George lived for several years in the Byzantine capital before being exiled with his family after serving as a diplomat under Emperor Alexios Komnenos. The family eventually found work in the Norman Kingdom of Sicily, where George would rise to prominence as a military officer and court official.

George's significance extends beyond his own achievements, as he helped pave the way for the multicultural society that became synonymous with the city-state. His legacy can be seen in the many cultural and religious exchanges that took place between the Byzantine and Norman rulers, which had a lasting impact on the region.

In 1151, George died under unclear circumstances, leaving behind a legacy that continues to fascinate historians today. Despite the passage of time, his contributions to Norman Sicily's transformation into a major power remain an important topic of study in the field of medieval history.
